title: Why Thanksgiving 'Food Coma' Isn't Turkey Tryptophan, Why 'Dessert Stomach' Is Real & Why Grandma's Chicken Soup Slowed Neutrophils — Debunking turkey tryptophan (~287 mg/100 g < chicken, pork, cheddar, soy) via Fernstrom & Wurtman (1971/1972 Science, PMID 5120086, 5077329) & Wurtman (2003 AJCN, PMID 12499331: N=9 human crossover 54% median Trp:LNAA swing), Wells (1997, PMID 9145937: N=18 fat/CCK fatigue) & Burdakov (2005/2006 Neuron, PMID 16731510: extracellular glucose silencing orexin via K2P channels); Rolls (1981, PMID 7267792, 7232526) & Kringelbach (2003 fMRI OFC, PMID 12967923) sensory-specific satiety + Minère & Fenselau (2025 Science, PMID 39946455: POMC->PVT beta-endorphin sugar circuit); Saketkhoo (1978 Chest, PMID 359266: N=15 soup 6.9->9.2 vs cold 7.3->4.5 mm/min) & Rennard (2000 Chest, PMID 11035691: Boyden neutrophil chemotaxis); PDBs 7DSQ, 7L1U, 4S0V, 8IC0.

teenKit.tldr: Turkey isn't actually what makes you sleepy after Thanksgiving dinner; your post-feast nap is driven by a massive carbohydrate insulin spike, dietary fats, and glucose shutting down your brain's wakefulness cells.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding these biological food hacks reveals how our bodies mechanically respond to sensory cues, heavy meals, and ancient remedies like chicken soup long before we even realize we're reacting.
keyTakeaways: Gram for gram, standard foods like chicken, pork, and cheddar cheese contain significantly more tryptophan than turkey, clearing the holiday bird of false accusations.
The mythical 'dessert stomach' is a real physiological circuit driven by sensory-specific satiety and brain reward pathways that instantly revive you when new flavors appear.
Grandma's chicken soup isn't just placebo water; scientific tests show it actively speeds up mucus flow and slows down immune neutrophils to reduce inflammation.

vocab.meaning: An essential amino acid often falsely blamed for holiday fatigue, though it loses out to other amino acids unless massive amounts of carbs are eaten.
The specific chemical wakefulness switch cells in your brain that get shut down and silenced when high levels of glucose hit them.
The neurological phenomenon where you feel completely full of one food type, but instantly hungry again when a completely new flavor or dessert is introduced.
Immune system white blood cells that rush to sites of infection and whose migration speed can be slowed down by compounds in chicken soup to ease inflammation.

quiz.question: Which everyday food actually contains a higher concentration of tryptophan than Thanksgiving turkey?
quiz.explanation: Standard blocks of cheddar cheese, chicken, and pork all pack higher amounts of tryptophan gram-for-gram than turkey.

quiz.question: What happens inside your brain to cause a food coma when a heavy, carbohydrate-loaded meal is digested?
options: Your brain cells freeze from cold food
Extracellular glucose silences your wakefulness-promoting orexin neurons via potassium channels
Your stomach physically expands until you pass out
Tryptophan directly coats your entire brain in a heavy blanket of protein
quiz.explanation: High blood glucose from carbs directly shuts down the brain's orexin wake-up neurons through tandem-pore potassium leak channels.

quiz.question: Why does the 'dessert stomach' phenomenon magically happen even when you feel completely stuffed?
options: Your stomach actually grows a secondary pouch for sugar
You digest savory food four times slower than sweet food
Sensory-specific satiety and reward circuits make you crave a brand new flavor profile
Your body runs out of room for protein and desperately demands empty calories
quiz.explanation: Switching sensory inputs and activating reward-based neural circuits instantly bypasses the feeling of fullness caused by the main course.
